notes: Country positions on solar radiation modification (SRM) and geoengineering for SRM Watch. Seed entries are illustrative samples; the scanner/analyst pipeline expands and corrects this over time. position: supportive | cautious | opposed | undeclared.

buckets.supportive: Supports research / open to governed exploration
buckets.cautious: Cautious — emphasises governance, moratoria pending oversight
buckets.opposed: Opposed — bans or restricts experiments / deployment

countries.summary: Federal science agencies have produced research plans and assessments treating solar radiation modification as a legitimate area of study, while stopping short of any deployment commitment.
key_actions: OSTP congressionally-mandated research plan on solar/atmosphere interventions (2023)
NOAA atmospheric science and monitoring programs

countries.summary: UK research funders have supported exploratory programmes on climate cooling approaches alongside calls for strong governance and transparency.
key_actions: ARIA exploratory climate / cooling research funding
Royal Society engagement on geoengineering governance

countries.summary: Switzerland has sought to put solar radiation modification on the multilateral agenda, proposing UN Environment Assembly consideration of an expert review and governance.
key_actions: Proposed UNEA resolution on solar radiation modification (2019, 2024)

countries.summary: Mexico announced steps to prohibit solar geoengineering experiments on its territory following an unauthorised private stratospheric aerosol release.
key_actions: Announced ban on solar geoengineering experimentation (2023)

countries.summary: Through the Convention on Biological Diversity, parties adopted a widely-cited decision discouraging climate-related geoengineering pending adequate scientific basis and governance.
key_actions: CBD decision establishing a de facto moratorium (2010, reaffirmed)
